summary: The Core Worlds course opens on a familiar map with Meridian enlarged at its center, and Professor Aven Teral makes the map itself the first object of suspicion.

panelPlan.text: Single full-page Academy lecture splash. Aven stands small beneath a wall-scale corridor map whose visual composition places Meridian at the obvious center, with Bastion Spire and other Core nodes radiating around it.
Integrate the exact lecture title into the wall display as designed Academy typography, leaving ample negative space and preserving the human scale of the cadets below.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY
dialogueInline.text: LECTURE ONE: MERIDIAN IS NOT THE CORE

directionInline: Treat DISPLAY entries as exact integrated lecture typography. No other readable environmental text or decorative labels.

summary: Aven asks what is wrong with the map; Lysa answers that nothing is, exposing how natural Meridian-centered geography feels to a Meridian-raised cadet.

panelPlan.text: Wide classroom panel: Aven faces the cadets with the Meridian-centered route map behind him.
Medium on Lysa studying the display with genuine concentration rather than searching for a trick.
Corin glances sideways at her answer; Jalen watches Aven instead of the map.
Close on Aven, almost amused but not mocking.

dialogueInline.text: What is wrong with this map?

summary: The cadets defend different ideas of the Core's center—Meridian, Bastion Spire, and the supply network—revealing that each is already answering a different question.

panelPlan.text: Lysa stands at the display and points to Meridian's dense route convergence.
Corin leans forward from his desk, countering with Bastion Spire's Fleet and repair infrastructure.
Jalen remains seated, tracing the outer green routes entering the Core rather than either highlighted node.
Aven lets the disagreement develop without rescuing them.

dialogueInline.text: Trade, population, administration, passenger traffic. They all converge on Meridian.
Ships do not get rebuilt on Meridian.
That does not make the drydock the center of civilization.
You both left out the routes feeding it.

summary: Aven turns the argument into a field assignment: the three cadets must leave the classroom and return with one defensible map of the Core.

panelPlan.text: Aven collapses the wall display to a blank field with only a few unlabelled route nodes.
He sets three temporary field passes on the front desk.
The cadets exchange looks as the assignment becomes physical rather than rhetorical.
Final narrow panel: Lysa snatches one pass first, competitive energy restored.

dialogueInline.text: By fourteen hundred, bring me one map of the Core.
I want you to discover what the word means before you print it.

summary: Crossing Bastion Spire's Crown Gallery, Corin makes the case that the Fleet's working and ceremonial heart is a stronger candidate for the Core's center than Meridian.

panelPlan.text: Large establishing panel: the three cadets move through the Crown Gallery Transit Walk beneath enormous banners while workers, travelers, and dock traffic flow through the same space.
Through a window, a major Fleet hull sits in drydock while maintenance crews swarm around it.
Corin walks backward for a few steps, gesturing at the working structure around them.
Lysa keeps moving, unimpressed by his local pride.

dialogueInline.text: Command, repair, launch, memorials, oath halls. This place keeps the Fleet alive.
And who pays for half of it?
Do not put that on the map.

summary: In the Anchor Markets, the cadets confront how thoroughly the Core's celebrated abundance is assembled from goods and people arriving from beyond its prestigious centers.

panelPlan.text: Dense but readable market panorama: Verge grain sacks, Core textiles, Shard-forged salvage, ship provisions, food stalls, commuters, and spacers share one vaulted concourse.
Jalen silently points out the origin diversity of goods without relying on readable labels.
Lysa scans the scene and starts taking notes on her slate.
They reach Ma Neris's bread stall where a queue has stopped moving.

dialogueInline.text: This is still a Core market.
Look at what is in it.
If you three are here to study the line, congratulations. It is getting longer.

summary: A grain hold stops Ma Neris's morning production, turning abstract interdependence into an ordinary breakfast problem inside the Core's ceremonial heart.

panelPlan.text: Ma checks a small status display beside nearly empty grain bins while finished loaves disappear from the counter.
Insert on the one exact status line, simple and legible.
Lysa looks from the hold notice to the crowded market around them.
Ma keeps working with the flour she has left.

dialogueInline.text: You do not keep local stock?
Meridian keeps enough to believe breakfast is guaranteed.

directionInline: The scripted BERTH 14 line is the only readable operational text in the stall.

summary: Ma serves the remaining Shatterbread and strips away the students' assumption that the food is merely a charming Core tradition.

panelPlan.text: Ma cuts one dense dark Shatterbread loaf into small pieces for the stalled queue rather than hoarding it behind the counter.
Lysa recognizes the famous food immediately.
Close on Ma's flour-marked hand pressing a piece into Lysa's palm.
Jalen tastes his piece; Corin studies the empty grain bin.

dialogueInline.text: My grandmother called it ration brick.
Nobody put that on the holiday banners.

summary: Ma gives the cadets the first usable rule for their map: chart what hurts when movement stops, not merely what looks important when everything works.

panelPlan.text: The queue starts moving again slowly as Ma switches to smaller portions and alternative stock.
Lysa adds supply lines to the group's draft map.
Jalen watches her add routes extending beyond the Core.
Ma points with her bread knife toward the market's freight side without pausing her work.

dialogueInline.text: So the map needs the food routes.
Your map needs whatever hurts when it stops.
That is not how maps work.
She is going in the bibliography.

summary: On the ferry toward Meridian, the planet's overwhelming scale restores Lysa's confidence that visual and cultural centrality must count for something.

panelPlan.text: Wide observation-window panel: Meridian fills much of the view, blue-green with luminous cities and violet storm belts.
Lysa stands at the glass while Corin and Jalen sit behind her with their half-finished map.
A civilian child nearby presses both hands to the window, reinforcing how naturally impressive the world is.
Close on Lysa, smiling despite herself.

dialogueInline.text: You can say what you want.
It still looks like the center.
From a ferry that left Bastion.

summary: At Core Spire Station, senior controller Tomas Kade rejects the students' central question as operationally meaningless until they define what their map is for.

panelPlan.text: Establish the busy Core Spire logistics floor with multiple human teams working real traffic and maintenance routing.
The cadets show Tomas their composite map on a handheld slate.
Tomas gives it one fast look while still tracking his own active board.
He hands the slate back without contempt.

dialogueInline.text: What is the center of the Core?
That is not a logistics question.

summary: Tomas cycles through four legitimate network views, each producing a different center and proving that geography changes with function.

panelPlan.text: First operations display: passenger movement makes Meridian visibly dominant.
Second: defense and heavy repair traffic concentrates around Bastion Spire.
Third: freight interchange emphasizes Core Spire and multiple less glamorous transfer nodes.
Fourth: emergency medical reserves create yet another pattern with distributed stockpiles.
End on the students' faces as none of the maps looks like their single clean diagram.

directionInline: Displays should communicate changing network emphasis visually without adding unscripted labels or legends.

summary: A live corridor hold interrupts the lesson, and the logistics floor instantly shifts from analysis to consequence as a verified route turns unsafe.

panelPlan.text: A green route on the main operations display snaps to red while one concise alert appears.
Tomas turns away from the cadets immediately and joins two controllers at a neighboring station.
Cargo and passenger route lines begin recomputing around the held segment.
The cadets step back, suddenly observing professionals rather than a demonstration.

dialogueInline.text: Medical transfer on C-19. Hold every entry.
Confirm the red at both beacons.

directionInline: Red must read as unsafe/held and green as verified safe. The C-19 alert is the only readable system alert.

summary: Tomas gives the students a scrubbed copy of the live routing problem, forcing them to make a timed recommendation while the real operations team works beside them.

panelPlan.text: Tomas flicks a sanitized duplicate of the affected network to a side workstation away from the live controls.
The cadets cluster around it, seeing a medical shipment stranded behind the red segment and several green alternatives of different lengths.
A small physical timer counts down without readable digits dominating the art.
Tomas points once, then returns to his real team.

dialogueInline.text: Training copy. You cannot touch traffic.
Nine minutes to the next verified window.
Tell me what you would do.

summary: Lysa's Meridian detour is safe and obvious but slow, exposing the cost of treating the most prominent hub as the default solution.

panelPlan.text: Lysa draws the detour through Meridian on the training display; the path is long but entirely green.
Jalen compares the new arrival time to the original direct route.
Corin checks the certified status of each segment and reluctantly sees Lysa's logic.
Lysa holds her ground.

dialogueInline.text: If the clinic can wait nine hours.
Do you have a safer route?

summary: Corin proposes using a Bastion maintenance tug to reopen the relay, but the solution consumes support assigned to a major Fleet launch, making infrastructure itself a contested resource.

panelPlan.text: Corin expands a maintenance layer and identifies a tug staged near Bastion Spire.
The tug's current assignment links visually to a carrier launch support window.
Jalen sees the conflict before Corin finishes.
The three cadets argue quietly while the real floor moves around them.

dialogueInline.text: Maintenance tug here. Send it to the relay, verify the lane, reopen C-19.
You just moved three thousand crew and a defense schedule.
Now we are finally mapping something.

summary: The professional routing team finds a third option through an overlooked maintenance spur, showing the cadets that the network's least prestigious infrastructure can become the most important route in a crisis.

panelPlan.text: On the live board, a thin maintenance spur flashes amber while sensors check it.
A controller confirms the spur; its line turns verified green.
The medical route redraws through it without passing Meridian or consuming the Bastion tug.
Tomas glances toward the cadets as the cargo starts moving again.

dialogueInline.text: Spur Six is clean. Move the medical transfer.

directionInline: The Spur Six verification is the only readable status text on this page.

summary: Lysa discovers that the successful route was always documented; it was invisible only to the prestige map she had mistaken for the system itself.

panelPlan.text: Lysa pulls up their public-facing Core map beside the operations layer and sees that Spur Six is absent from the simplified view.
Tomas closes one alert and finally gives the cadets his full attention.
Corin points to the maintenance layer, vindicated but thoughtful rather than triumphant.
Jalen adds the thin spur to their own map.

dialogueInline.text: Why is that not on the Core atlas?
It is on the operations atlas.
Nobody puts maintenance spurs on monuments.
Maybe cadets should learn there is more than one map.

summary: Back at the Academy, the group's single assignment has become three incompatible but defensible maps: civic movement, repair capacity, and survival supply.

panelPlan.text: Three distinct student maps fill the wall: Lysa's civic/passenger network, Corin's repair and maintenance network, Jalen's food and supply network.
Aven walks slowly across them while the cadets stand beneath their own work.
Lysa looks mildly annoyed at the assignment's impossible wording.
Aven turns back to the class.

summary: Aven names the real lesson: a map is an answer to a question, and danger begins when one useful answer becomes the unquestioned picture of the whole civilization.

panelPlan.text: Aven overlays the three student maps so their centers visibly fail to coincide.
Lysa looks back at the original Meridian-centered map from the morning.
Jalen folds his arms, considering how often maps arrive with authority already attached.
Corin sees maintenance lines nearly disappear beneath the prettier layers.

dialogueInline.text: Passenger map. Repair map. Food map. Each answers a different question.
And the one with Meridian in the middle?
A useful answer that learned to call itself the question.

summary: For the final exercise, Aven gives the cadets one guaranteed corridor window and three urgent claims on it—medicine, repair capability, and evacuation—forcing them to choose what continuity means in practice.

panelPlan.text: Aven replaces the map with three clean visual case tiles: medical cargo, relay-control parts, and civilian evacuees, all converging on one safe green transit window before a predicted closure.
He places a physical decision slate on the desk in front of the three cadets.
Lysa reads the manifests twice.
Corin and Jalen realize there is no hidden fourth route this time.

dialogueInline.text: Medicine for a clinic. Relay parts that may reopen two routes tomorrow. Forty-eight civilians who can evacuate now.
There is always a moment when the clever answer runs out.

directionInline: Do not invent manifest labels or statistics beyond the exact dialogue. The three choices should be visually clear through objects and people, not extra text.

summary: The cadets stop searching for a symbolic winner and build a network response: prioritize repair parts while using the Core's reserves and prestige capacity to mitigate the human costs elsewhere.

panelPlan.text: The cadets argue around the decision slate, no one sitting now.
Jalen taps the medicine case; Corin points to the relay parts; Lysa studies the wider map instead of either object.
Lysa begins moving resource markers from Meridian and a ceremonial Fleet launch window into the plan.
All three lean over the slate and sign the same decision.
Aven reads it without giving them an easy smile.

dialogueInline.text: People are waiting on the medicine.
If the relay stays dead, more people wait tomorrow.
Pull Meridian's reserve stock for the clinic. Delay the ceremonial launch and use its escort capacity for the evacuation.

summary: On the ferry after class, Meridian still looks like the center; the difference is that the cadets now recognize the viewpoint built into that impression.

panelPlan.text: Quiet evening ferry panel: Meridian glows through the observation glass, still visually enormous and beautiful.
The three cadets sit together with their now-crowded multi-layer map between them.
Lysa looks from the planet to the map.
Final wide panel pulls back enough to show other orbital lights and route nodes around Meridian rather than isolating it as the only meaningful object.

dialogueInline.text: It still looks like the center.
Tomorrow we draw it from somewhere else.

summary: Closing Academy teaser converts the lesson into the next problem: safe corridors are scarce civic capacity, and allocation determines who moves and who waits.

panelPlan.text: Single full-page editorial/Academy teaser. Use a clean network image with several equally weighted Core nodes joined by verified green corridors; no node should visually dominate the page as an obvious universal center.
Reserve strong negative space for the exact teaser copy. This is back-matter framing, not an additional character scene.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A safe route is not just geometry.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It is time, food, medicine, trade, authority—and the decision that someone else will wait.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Rex Fleet Academy: The Core Worlds continues.

directionInline: Treat all CAPTION entries as exact integrated editorial typography, not speech balloons. No other readable environmental text.
